headline: Welcome to the live coverage of La Vuelta 26!
subtext: The 81st edition of La Vuelta starts in Monaco, home to a historic Gran Salida. As the Principality becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, powerhouses gear for a spectacular first battle. La Roja is at stakes on a 9.4 km individual time-trial set to establish the first hierarchy and visit Monaco’s most iconic landmarks. Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) will get the action going, at 16:17, and Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) will be the last rider off the ramp, at 19:20.

headline: Welcome to Monaco
subtext: For the seventh time in 81 editions, and the fourth time in five years, La Vuelta is setting off from outside Spain. After Lisbon (1997 and 2024), Assen (2009), Nîmes (2017), Utrecht (2022) and Piemonte (2025), it is now Monaco’s turn. With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009). Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. A few weeks later, Cancellara was the first leader of the 2009 Vuelta after an ITT in Assen (the Netherlands).

headline: A very special day for Langellotti
subtext: The start in Monaco features a very special participant: Monegasque rider Victor Langelloti (XDS Astana), the only rider from the Principality in the current professional peloton, who will begin his third appearance in La Vuelta on home soil. “As a Monegasque, it is an honour to be able to ride La Vuelta at home and a source of pride to be able to wear this jersey”, says Langellotti, who won both the road race and the ITT at the national championships. “In 2009, when the Tour de France started from here, as a local cyclist I was able to accompany Alberto Contador’s Astana team at the team presentation. Now, riding with them and being able to start La Vuelta at home is incredible – something I could never have imagined.”

headline: Many local figures: Pogacar, Carapaz, Pedersen…
subtext: Although Langelloti is the only rider from Monaco in the current professional peloton, there are many cyclists who are normally based in the Principality, and several of them will be taking part in this opening time trial. The list begins with Tadej Pogacar, who made no secret the Gran Salida in Monaco was a key factor for him to participate, and goes on with Richard Carapaz, Mads Pedersen, Hugo Houle, Oscar Chamberlain, Alessandro Covi, Steven Kruijswijk, Tobias Johanessen, Ed Dunbar… “It’s quite simple: Monaco is the perfect place to ride the bike”, Primoz Roglic explains.

headline: From Uriarte to Roglic
subtext: The opening ITT of La Vuelta 26 is the perfect occasion to get familiar with the field of this 81st edition and see who will bring the race to life en route to Granada. Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) is set to be the first rider on course, from 16:17, as he participates in his first Grand Tour. At 24, he is in his third season as a professional, after developing with Lizarte, Kern Pharma’s feeder club. He will be followed at 16:18 later by the much more experienced Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL), lining up for the sixth time at the start of La Vuelta. The 184 contenders of this edition will start every minute, finishing wit some of the most awaited champions in this edition. Belgian icon Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) will go at 19:17. He will be followed by Spain’s rising star Ivan Romeo (Movistar). After them, two Slovenian giants will close the action: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG), starting at 19:19, and Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), a minute after his compatriot.

headline: Following the tracks of Formula 1 legends
subtext: “A very urban, very technical route, with plenty of speed and changes of pace”: this is how Kiko Garcia, technical director of La Vuelta 26, describes the route of the first stage. “It’s a time trial that obviously won’t decide the winner of La Vuelta, but it will show who is best equipped in terms of technique, explosive power and the ability to manoeuvre on a city circuit.” The route will be relatively flat, with an elevation gain of 59 metres over a total distance of 9.4 kilometres. Motorsport enthusiasts will recognise the Monaco Grand Prix circuit, which forms a significant part of the route. The riders will pass through the Place du Casino, the famous Fairmont bend and the Louis II tunnel before arriving on Boulevard Albert 1er, where the victory cries of drivers such as Ayrton Senna, Alain Prost, Michael Schumacher, Fernando Alonso, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli still echo.

headline: La Vuelta 26 is ON!
subtext: Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) just rolled off the start ramp. He will be followed in a minute by CHris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL). Then, it will be Reuben THompson (Lotto Intermarché), Cesar Macias (Burgos Burpellet BH), Darren van Bekkum (XDS Astana)...

headline: The 36th edition of La Vuelta to begin with an ITT
subtext: Today marks the 36th time La Vuelta starts with an ITT (in 81 editions). On the first occasion, in 1948, Bernardo Ruiz and Julian Berrendero were tied after the opening ITT in Madrid. More recently, Brandon McNulty took the first La Roja through an ITT in Lisbon in 2024, three years after Primoz Roglic dominated the opening ITT in Burgos. The list of riders who took the first leader’s jersey inn ITT features icons such as Luis Ocaña (1969, 1970), Eddy Merckx (1973), Freddy Maertens (1977), Bernard Hinault (1978), Fabian Cancellara (2009)…

headline: Kaden Groves begins his 4th La Vuelta
subtext: Winner of the points standings in 2023 and 2024, the Australian versatile sprinter has won stages in each of his previous participations: - in Cabo de Gata (stage 11) in 2022 - in Tarragona (4), Borriana (5), and Madrid (21) in 2023 - in Ourem (2), Villablino (14), and Santander (17) in 2024 He also won the points standings 2023 and 2024.

headline: 23 La Vuelta stage winners
subtext: 15 stage wins - Primoz Roglic 7 - Kaden Groves 6 - Magnus Cort 4 - Mads Pedersen, Jay Vine 3 - Wout van Aert, Richard Carapaz, Jesus Herrada, Tadej Pogacar 2 - Pablo Castrillo, Eddie Dunbar, Sepp Kuss 1 - Joao Almeida, Urko Berrade, David de la Cruz, Alberto Dainese, Lennard Kämna, Andreas Kron, Stefan Küng, Mikel Landa, Alexey Lutsenko, Enric Mas, Ben Turner

headline: 10 ITT champions at the start
subtext: 16:37 - Orluis Aular, Venezuela 17:29 - Sergio Chumil, Guatemala 17:53 - Yevgeniy Fedorov, Asia + Kazakhstan 18:32 - Pablo Castrillo, Spain 18:33 - Jay Vine, Australia 18:39 - Victor Langellotti, Monaco 18:57 - Finn Fisher-Black, New Zealand 19:06 - Alex Kirsch, Luxembourg 19:08 - Ethan Hayter, Great Britain 19:20 - Primoz Roglic, Slovenia

headline: First benchmarks
subtext: Ten riders have made it to the finish, and Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) currently holds the best time: 11'38''. But Kaden Groves (Alpecin-Premier Tech) and Mathias Norsgaard (Movistar) are just ahead of him at the intermediate checkpoint (km 5.6).

headline: Groves behind Leknessund at the finish
subtext: The Australian sprinter was 0.3 second behind the Norwegian powerhouse at the checkpoint, but he finished a second and a half behind.

headline: Norsgaard in the hotseat; watch out for Labrosse!
subtext: Mathias Norsgaard (Movistar) finishes with a margin of 1 second on Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility). But Jordan Labrosse (Decathlon CMA CGM) went flying over the first 5.6km: 6'41'', ten seconds faster than Norsgaard! Orluis Aular (Movistar) is in between (+6'').

headline: Carapaz sets off
subtext: The winner of the KOM standings in 2022, Richard Carapaz is one of eleven contenders in this edition to have already taken home a distinctive jersey, and one of seven to have stood on the final overall podium. There are two former winners of La Vuelta: Primoz Roglic (2019, 2020, 2021, 2024) and Sepp Kuss (2023). Enric Mas, Joao Almeida, Jack Haig and Tadej Pogacar are the others top 3 finishers.Primoz Roglic also won the points standings (2019, 2020). So did Mads Pedersen (2022, 2025) and Kaden Groves (2023, 2024). Winners of the KOM standings: Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (2020), Richard Carapaz (2022), Jay Vine (2024, 2025). Winners of the young riders standings: Enric Mas (2018, 2020), Tadej Pogacar (2019), Mattias Skjelmose (2024), Matthew Riccitello (2025).

headline: Labrosse impresses: 11'20''
subtext: The Decathlon CMA CGM rider takes the best time 17 seconds ahead of Mathias Norsgaard (Movistar)!

headline: Aular just behind Labrosse
subtext: The Venzuelian trails by 0.17 second at the finish!

headline: 29 nations in the peloton
subtext: 30 riders - Spain 23 - France 18 - Belgium 13 - Italy 12 - Australia, Great Britain 9 - Netherlands 8 - Denmark 7 - Germany, Norway, Slovenia 5 - Colombia, USA 4 - Austria 3 - Luxembourg, New Zealand, Switzerland 2 - Kazakhstan, Ireland, Portugal 1 - Canada, Czechia, Ecuador, Eritrea, Guatemala, Hungary, Mexico, Monaco, Venezuela

headline: Kuss starts his third Grand Tour of the year
subtext: The USA climber was 13th in the Giro d’Italia, where he accompanied Jonas Vingegaard to the overall victory, and 13th in the Tour de France, where he won the opening TTT with Visma-Lease a Bike and animated the two days finishing at Alpe d’Huez (4th on stage 19, 3rd the next day). This is the second time Kuss participates in the Grand Tours in one season. Last time, in 2023, he even claimed La Roja as the overall winner of La Vuelta!

headline: 42 finishers
subtext: Matthew Riccitello (Decathlon CMA CGM) just crossed the line with the 13th best time (+23''). Jordan Labrosse (Decathlon CMA CGM) still holds the best time, 0.17 second ahead of Orluis Aular (Movistar). Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility) completes the curent top 3 (+8'') ahead of Richard Carapaz (+10'').

headline: Johannessen and Skjelmose go hard
subtext: Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility) now has the third best time at the finish: 11'25'' (+5''). Will he be beaten by Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek)? The Danish GC contender set the second best time at the intermediate checkpoint (+4'') just ahead of Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious).

headline: Brennan is off to a flying start!
subtext: Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) is six seconds faster than Jordan Labrosse (Decathlon CMA CGM) across the checkpoint (km 5.7). Meanwhile, Carlos Rodriguez (3rd, +4'') and Mattias Skjelmose (5th, +6'') take place in the top 5 at the finish.

headline: Brennan takes the best time ahead of De Pestel
subtext: Sander De Pestel (Decathlon CMA CGM) finished with a time of 11'15'', a couple of seconds ahead of his French teammate Jordan Labrosse. But Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) immediately bettered this benchmark: 11'13''.

headline: The youngest participant in La Vuelta 26 followed by Onley
subtext: Born in 2006, Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) is the youngest rider at the start of the 81st La Vuelta. He is 20 years and 154 days old today, four months younger than Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché). Pablo Torres (UAE Emirates XRG) and Sente Sentjens (Alpecin-Premier Tech) are the other two 20 years old participants. The latter will celebrate his 21st birthday on 2 September (stage 11). One minute after Ormzel, Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) rides La Vuelta for the second time. He was also 20 years old when he first participated, in 2023. That year, he won the opening TTT in Barcelona but had to withdraw early in the race. This year, he was set to lead Netcompany Ineos in the Tour before crashing on the final stage of the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes.

headline: Kluckers started faster than Brennan
subtext: After 5.6 km, Arthur Kluckers (Tudor) is 2 seconds ahead of Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) and 8 seconds faster than Jordan Labrosse (Decathlon CMA CGM).

headline: Best time for Kluckers: 11'08''
subtext: The former Luxembourg ITT champion went 5 seconds faster than Brennan.

headline: Can Küng win the opening ITT of La Vuelta?
subtext: The Swiss powerhouse, starting at 18:17, is one of two riders to have already won a La Vuelta ITT. It was on the last day of the 2024 edition, in Madrid. Primoz Roglic won the opening and the closing ITTs of the 2021 edition, as well as stage 10 in 2019 and stage 13 in 2020.

headline: Chamberlain edges Kluckers out of the hotseat
subtext: Oscar Chamberlain covered the 9.4 km in 11'06'', two seconds faster than Kluckers. That makes three Decathlon CMA CGM riders in the top 5 alongside Sander De Pestel (4th, +9'') and Jordan Labrosse (5th, +14'').

headline: 3rd best time for Oliveira
subtext: The top 5 with 115 riders at the finish: 1. Oscar Chamberlain (Decathlon CMA CGM), 11'06'' 2. Arthur Kluckers (Tudor), +2'' 3. Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), +5'' 4. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike), +7'' 5. Sander De Pestel (Decathon CMA CGM), +9''

headline: Romele in the top 3, Küng 4th
subtext: The top 5 with 122 riders at the finish: 1. Oscar Chamberlain (Decathlon CMA CGM), 11'06'' 2. Arthur Kluckers (Tudor), +2'' 3. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana), +4'' 4. Stefan Küng (Tudor), +5'' 5. Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), +5''

headline: Jay Vine’s sixth La Vuelta
subtext: The Australian star built a very special relationship with La Vuelta over the years. Back in 2021, it was his first Grand Tour and he most notably impressed with a 3rd place at Pico Villuercas despite crashing on that day due to a mishap with his team car. The next year, he claimed two stage wins and was wearing the polka dot jersey when he crashed out of the race in the final week. He also had to abandon the 2023 edition before finally conquering the KOM standings in 2024. Last year, he took home the polka dot jersey again and also won two mountain stages.

headline: Langellotti starts at home
subtext: Victor Langellotti is the local rider of the Gran Salida, and the only Monegasque rider in the current professional peloton. This is his third La Vuelta after he participated in 2022 with Burgos-BH and in 2025 with Ineos. He will spend the next three weeks wearing the Monaco national champion jersey, both in time trials and in road race stages… unless he takes a distinctive jersey as he did in 2022 when he led the KOM standings for three stages.

headline: Bisiaux ahead of Chamberlain!
subtext: With a time of 11'05'', the French youngster is 0.75 second faster than his Decathlon CMA CGM teammate Oscar Chamberlain!

headline: 5th best time for Jay Vine
subtext: The Australian powerhouse trails by 6'' on the line.

headline: Thornley even faster than Bisiaux
subtext: Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) had a very strong second part of the ITT to set the best time, 11'02'', three seconds ahead of Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM).

headline: Tarling sets off
subtext: The British powerhouse might be the purest TT talent starting La Vuelta 26. At 22 years old, he’s already won the national and continental titles, as well as a Grand Tour stage (in the Giro 2025), and stood on the podium of the Worlds (3rd in 2023) in addition to his success on the track. Regardless of his result today, one can only respect his decision to race eight days after his younger brother Finlay Tarling died in a tragic accident. A few days later, the family announced Joshua’s grandfather had also passed away.

headline: Best time for Tarling at km 5.6
subtext: The British star averages 51.4 km/h so far and is 1'' ahead of Kluckers' benchmark.

headline: Tarling takes the best time at the finish: 11'01''
subtext: The British powerhouse covered the 9.4 km at 51.2 km/h to beat Callum Thornley by one second!

headline: 6th time for Fisher-Black, 14th for Almeida
subtext: The New Zeland ITT champion was 0.3 second behind Tarling at km 5.6, but he eventually reached the finish with a gap of 6 seconds. Joao Almeida (UAE Emirates XRG) finished 14'' behind Tarling. That makes him the best GC contender at the moment.

headline: 10 riders remain in the start area
subtext: With Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) on the start ramp, only ten riders are yet to start La Vuelta 26. The French youngster will be followed by Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek), Roman Ermakov (Bahrain Victorious), Ben Turner (Netcompany Ineos), David de la Cruz (Pinarello Q36.5), Callum Scotson (Decathlon CMA CGM), Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), Ivan Romeo (Movistar), Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG), and eventually Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), starting at 19:20.

headline: Hayter threatens Tarling's benchmark
subtext: At km 5.6, the British ITT champion is 2.2 seconds faster than his compatriot.

headline: Wout van Aert (Visma | Lease a Bike)
Hayter beats Tarling at the finish
subtext: Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) is the first rider to go under 11 minutes: 10'57'', 4 seconds ahead of Josh Tarling (Netcompany Ineos). Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) completes a fully British top 3 (+5'').

headline: Pogacar and Roglic have started
subtext: The Slovenian icons are the last riders off the ramp.

headline: 2nd best time for Pogacar at km 5.6
subtext: The Slovenian is 2.18'' behind Hayter and 0.02'' ahead of Tarling.

headline: Pogacar edges Hayter with the smallest margin!
subtext: 10'57''14 for the Slovenian... That's 0.09 second faster than the British champion!

headline: Tadej Pogacar wins stage 1 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: 1. Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG), 10’57’’ 2. Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), +0’’ 3. Josh Tarling (Netcompany Ineos), +4’’ 4. Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), +5’’ 5. Christophe Laporte (Visma-Lease a Bike), +6’’
